digest.component_or_area: tickets-branch push, delivery signal on async/library/MCP paths
propositions: Failed tickets-branch pushes rejected by pre-receive hooks are undeliverable: the async path discards stderr via DEVNULL+start_new_session, library embedders have no handler installed, MCP servers write to server stderr not agent-visible tool result, and reconciler subprocess logs under wrong root

A durable marker in the git dir (not working tree) records push failures at the single _raise_if_strict choke point and is cleared on successful push, making the failure observable on all four surfaces regardless of logging handler or stderr capture

The MCP write-tool surfaces (11 tools returning -> str) now advertise a push_status field alongside result, and rebar.push_status() provides the library surface, both reporting state (ok|pending) with reason, detail, remote_ref, unpushed count, and since timestamp

Terminal failures (reject, transport failure, lock timeout, commit phase failures, merge/recovery blocks, policy decline) are recorded as pending; non-failures (push-disabled, async-unobservable, remote-not-found, invalid-destination) are not recorded to avoid alarm fatigue on local-only stores

The best-effort contract is preserved: push_tickets_branch still returns None, never raises on default path, no CLI exit code changes, marker write failure does not fail the write, and working-tree git status remains byte-identical after a failed push

The test suite (59 tests driving real rejecting origins with real pre-receive hooks, no mocks) validates all four limbs: async polls marker on 60s/0.1s deadline, library via push_status() with no handler, MCP via tool result field, and reconciler via same disk-recording mechanism regardless of logger root
